deep.reconstruction:
The page is about the fibre sequence (Puppe sequence) of pointed spaces. It treats the whole sequence as one diagram shaped like a staircase, built entirely from homotopy-cartesian squares. All arrows point leftward and downward, and e denotes the base point (the terminal pointed object).

(1) First diagram. Start with f: X -> Y.
- Z is the homotopy fibre of f. This is the square [e -> Y <- X, Z].
- Pasting a second square [e <- ΩY -> Z, e] shows that ΩY is the fibre of g: Z -> X. The connecting map is h: ΩY -> Z.
- A third square [ΩX, ΩY, e] gives the next term.
- The top square [e <- ΩZ, ΩY <- ΩX] identifies ΩZ with the fibre of Ωf: ΩX -> ΩY.
The pasting lemma for homotopy pullbacks makes every composite rectangle cartesian. Each composite rectangle with e at two corners is a loop-space or fibre identification.

(2) Second diagram. The staircase is extended up to Ω^3 and Ω^4 levels. The arrows are labelled f, g, h, Ωf, Ωg, Ωh, Ω^2 f, Ω^2 g, Ω^2 h, Ω^3 f, Ω^3 g, Ω^3 h. Each map of the sequence appears alternately as a horizontal and a vertical arrow. The infinite staircase, read along its diagonal, is the fibre sequence
  Y <- X <- Z <- ΩY <- ΩX <- ΩZ <- Ω^2 Y <- ...
The periodicity (Y, X, Z) -> (ΩY, ΩX, ΩZ) is visible as translating the staircase by three steps.

(3) Small sketches.
- 'P <- Q' with a vertical arrow: a generic square or arrow.
- A sketch of the staircase as an indexing poset. The circled entries are the e's (the boundary, where the diagram is required to be trivial) together with X and Y. Lines bound a region, apparently asking which part of the coherent diagram determines the rest, i.e. a cofinality or Kan-extension statement.
- A dashed diagram: e, X, Y with diagonal arrows from e. This apparently shows how the square defining Z arises by extension from the arrow X -> Y alone.

(4) Bottom line. The full sequence is written linearly, with zig-zag arrows to and from e above and below. Each zig-zag marks that two consecutive maps compose through the point, i.e. a chosen null-homotopy. So the sequence is recorded as a coherent diagram of composable maps with coherent null-homotopies of length-2 composites.

Purpose: in 1983 (the period of Pursuing Stacks) Grothendieck appears to be working out how the fibre/Puppe sequence, and implicitly a triangulated-like structure, is encoded by a single coherent diagram on a staircase-shaped index category with trivial boundary. The whole diagram would be determined by Kan extension from the single arrow f.

This is precisely the mechanism later used in derivator theory to construct the canonical (pre)triangulation of a stable or pointed derivator: Franke's systems of triangulated diagram categories, Maltsiniotis, and Groth's 'Derivators, pointed derivators and stable derivators' (2013). The latter uses grids of bicartesian squares with zero boundary.
errors: Signs are ignored. When a cartesian square is read transposed, the induced map on loops is the inverse loop. In the honest staircase some maps should therefore be -Ωf, -Ωg, etc. (or Ωf precomposed with loop inversion). This is exactly the sign subtlety in the rotation axiom for triangulations; the labels here are written without signs.

Some labels in the second diagram are internally inconsistent. Since h: ΩY -> Z, the arrow labelled Ω^3 h must have source Ω^4 Y, but the top right entry looks like 'Ω^3 Y'. It is probably Ω^4 Y written hastily.
The placement of the vertical labels (Ω^2 h, Ω^2 f, Ωg, etc.) does not consistently sit on the arrow with the correct source and target. It is a sketch, not a checked diagram.

ideas.what: Fibre/Puppe sequence obtained by pasting homotopy-cartesian squares with trivial corners
ideas.modern_name: Fibre sequence via pasting lemma for homotopy pullbacks
ideas.usually_credited_to: Puppe (1958), Nomura; standard (e.g. Hovey, Model Categories, Ch. 6)
ideas.where_published: Possibly touched on in Pursuing Stacks / Les Dérivateurs; not verified

ideas.what: The entire fibre sequence encoded as one coherent diagram on a staircase-shaped index category with point/zero boundary, translation by three steps giving Ω
ideas.modern_name: Staircase/grid diagrams of bicartesian squares with zero boundary used to define the (pre)triangulated structure on a pointed/stable derivator
ideas.where_published: Les Dérivateurs (1990–91) discusses derivators but I am unsure whether this staircase construction appears there

ideas.what: Consecutive composites in the sequence equipped with coherent null-homotopies (zig-zags to e)
ideas.modern_name: Coherent fibre sequences / cofibre sequences as diagrams with coherent nullhomotopies

missed.claim: In 1983 Grothendieck already uses the staircase-of-cartesian-squares picture: the fibre sequence is a coherent diagram with trivial boundary on a staircase poset. He apparently considers which region of the index category determines the rest. This is the mechanism later made into the theorem that pointed/stable derivators carry canonical (pre)triangulations. The page documents an early, unstable (Ω, pointed spaces) version of that idea in Grothendieck's own hand, several years before Les Dérivateurs.
missed.quote: Y <- X <- Z <- ΩY <- ΩX <- ΩZ <- Ω^2 Y <- Ω^2 X <- Ω^2 Z <- Ω^3 Y <- (with zig-zags to e)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority/genealogy for the derivator approach to triangulations, usually credited to Franke, Maltsiniotis and Groth. It is mathematically standard now, so mostly of historical interest.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is the standard Puppe sequence. The notable feature is the coherent-staircase viewpoint with trivial boundary, an early derivator-style encoding of fibre sequences in 1983. It anticipates later work but is not itself a new result, and signs are not treated.
transcription_corrections: Second diagram, top right: the source of Ω^3 h should be Ω^4 Y, not Ω^3 Y (the handwriting is ambiguous).
The isolated 'P <- Q' has a vertical arrow above Q (a P over Q), forming a small corner/square sketch.
The middle line 'Y <- X <- Z <- ΩY <-' is a first attempt at the full sequence written at the bottom of the page.
The circled-staircase sketch has circled e's along the boundary and circled X, Y, plus ruled lines marking a sub-region; the transcription omits this.
